hypotheses.name: Structured Entailment Gate
hypotheses.description: Parse query and evidence into subject/predicate/object/temporal/certainty/polarity tuples and require an aligned supporting tuple.

hypotheses.name: Query Decomposition plus Evidence Coverage
hypotheses.description: Decompose the query into atomic mandatory requirements and require complete coverage across one or more evidence propositions.

hypotheses.name: Evidence Consistency Graph
hypotheses.description: Represent requirements, supporting propositions, temporal validity, contradiction and supersession as a graph; answer only when every requirement has a conflict-free support path.

hypotheses.name: Counterfactual Answerability Test
hypotheses.description: Remove high-overlap query cues and test whether answer-bearing proposition content still remains.

hypotheses.name: Hybrid Deterministic plus Local NLI
hypotheses.description: Use deterministic structured verification first and a frozen local NLI/LLM verifier only for unresolved cases, failing closed on parse errors.

selected_architecture.name: Atomic Requirement Evidence Graph
selected_architecture.rationale: This composition directly targets the observed any-support weakness by making answerability an all-required proposition-coverage problem. It preserves candidate-v2 ranking as retrieval only, separates lexical relevance from proof, permits multi-memory composition, and represents contradictions/temporal validity explicitly. H4 is retained only as a query-echo/near-duplicate guard. H5 is deferred because deterministic implementation is sufficient for the preregistered first Candidate-v5 identity and is easier to reproduce at zero monetary cost.
identity_boundary_from_candidate_v4: No reuse of candidate_v4 answerability_signature or _candidate_support semantics.
Candidate-v5 decomposes query requirements before examining retrieved evidence.
Candidate-v5 builds proposition coverage across multiple evidence items rather than accepting based on any supporting memory.
Contradiction and temporal resolution are graph-level properties, not timestamp/value heuristics applied after support acceptance.
Lexical relevance score is unavailable to the verifier except for the ordered list of frozen candidate-v2 memory IDs.
